content.text: Missing invariant: min_i is the minimum of a[s..i]. That's a bridge failure (invariant too weak to imply ensures).

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop in find_min_index only has invariants bounding i and min_i; nothing records that a[min_i] is the minimum of the scanned range a[s..i). So at loop exit (i == e) the invariants do not imply the postcondition forall k :: s <= k < e ==> a[min_i] <= a[k]. Adding the invariant forall k :: s <= k < i ==> a[min_i] <= a[k] (initially vacuous, maintained by the body's update) closes the gap."}
EOF
sed -i '17a\    invariant forall k: int :: s <= k < i ==> a[min_i] <= a[k]' program.dfy
sed -n 14,20p program.dfy; dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
The program now verifies: `dafny verify program.dfy` reports 6 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** the loop in `find_min_index` had invariants that only kept `i` and `min_i` within range. Nothing said that `a[min_i]` was the smallest value seen so far. When the loop ends (`i == e`), Dafny only knows the invariants plus the exit condition, and those don't imply the third `ensures` (line 9). So this is an **invariant / bridge** failure. The counterexample shows the gap: `min_i` stays at 1541 even though the invariants never rule out that some other element in `[s, e)` is smaller.

**Fix:** I added one invariant at `program.dfy:18`:
```dafny
invariant forall k: int :: s <= k < i ==> a[min_i] <= a[k]
```
It holds trivially on entry, when the range is empty. The loop body keeps it true, because `min_i` moves to `i` whenever `a[i] <= a[min_i]`. At exit, with `i == e`, it is exactly the postcondition.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before making the edit, and its content still matches what the fix showed.
